what_happened.line: The committee voted unanimously to approve its cable subscriber and revenue numbers for use if asked at town meeting.
Members described revenue as close to flat, comparing one payment in 2019 to one in 2022, against a statewide decline in cable subscribers.
Most of the meeting went to future studio space, with a member presenting rental, metal-building, mortgage and operating-cost estimates; no resolution was reached.
The manager asked for a line item transfer because the purchase order for a portable AV switcher ran out.
The committee asked whether its fund, largely from Comcast capital payments, can go toward a building; no answer was available.

why_it_matters: The committee's cable fee is a share of video revenue only, so the subscriber trend it described governs the money available for a public-access studio.
Whether that fund is restricted to equipment or can pay for a building is unanswered, and it bears on how a new studio would be paid for, possibly including town money.
watch_next: Next meeting May 2nd at five o'clock, with future studio space on the agenda.
An answer on whether the PACC fund is restricted to studio equipment, which the building committee asked for.
